body:
## Summary

Various corrections and updates to docs:


- On the Slurm backends, a crashed ensemble member looked like a successful one.
  Generated batch scripts ended in `exit 0`, so the job's exit status was always
  0, and `job_status` polled `squeue`, which stops listing a job once it
  finishes. No Slurm code path returned `FAILED`, which left `log_member_error`
  unreachable there. (PBS did return `FAILED`, for substate 93.) Job state now
  comes from `sacct` once the job has left the queue, an unrecognized `sacct`
  state counts as a failure, and a member that did not write a "completed"
  checkpoint counts as failed whatever the scheduler says. A `squeue` that
  cannot reach the controller returns nothing at all, which reads the same as a
  job that has left the queue, so its exit status is consulted and the job stays
  `RUNNING`.
- `initialize` overwrote iteration 1 on restart, pairing the output of
  checkpointed members with parameters they never ran with. It now keeps the
  stored process and errors when the one it is given describes a different
  calibration: a different ensemble size, observations, covariance shape, or
  process.
- `load_latest_ekp` returned `nothing` for directories produced by `calibrate`
  (it probed `iteration_000`).
- `analyze_residual` read the noise covariance from the last iteration rather
  than the requested one. The metadata helpers had the matching bug in the other
  direction: they wrapped the iteration back into the first epoch, so from the
  second epoch on a shuffling minibatcher labelled the residual with the
  variables of a different minibatch.
- `calibrate` returned the stored first iteration when the loop had nothing left
  to run, which looks like a calibration that never updated. A calibration the
  EKP scheduler terminated now also stays terminated, rather than resuming on
  the parameters the terminated update left behind.
- `set_worker_loggers` ignored its argument.
- `SlurmConfig` rewrote underscores in directive values, so
  `:partition => "gpu_debug"` emitted `gpu-debug`.
- PBS reported queued and held jobs as running.
- The covariance estimators could hand EKP a singular matrix with no
  diagnostic. `SeasonalDiagonalCovariance` now names the variable behind a zero
  or `NaN` variance. `SVDplusDCovariance` warns when its D term has a zero while
  the SVD term is rank deficient, which covers both its own defaults and the
  case where only `model_error_scale` is set and a sample mean is zero.
- `cancel_jobs_at_exit` was defined and documented but never called, so killing
  a calibration left every submitted member running. It is now registered, and
  cancels the jobs that are still running.

### Breaking API changes

One `calibrate` method instead of three. A `failure_rate` used by all
backends, and a `job_timeout` on the HPC backends whose clock starts when a job
leaves the queue. `get_backend` renamed `backend_type` (it returns a type, not a
backend `calibrate` accepts) and `default_worker_pool` renamed
`calibration_worker_pool` (it collided with `Distributed`), both with the old
name kept as a deprecation. `YAML` is no longer a dependency and `Dates` is
test-only. `terminated_iteration` is new.

### Docs

New Concepts and Troubleshooting pages, a job-status section in Backends, a
README following the [DeveloperGuides](https://github.com/CliMA/DeveloperGuides)
documentation policy, and a tutorial that runs a simple damped oscillator
instead of ClimaAtmos. `linkcheck` runs on CI as a warning, so an upstream
outage does not fail a pull request.

Closes #205, #265, #288, #297, #358.

Sorry, it's one large PR. I had a block of time to work on it, and won't have
time to shepherd through several smaller PRs, which would have been more
review-friendly. The largest changes are in 
the docs; they are best reviewed by reading the entire built docs.

This is co-produced with Claude.

Bumps [julia-actions/setup-julia](https://github.com/julia-actions/setup-julia) from 2 to 3.
Release notes

Sourced from julia-actions/setup-julia's releases.

v3.0.0

:warning: Breaking Changes, and Migration Guide for v2 ⟶ v3

  1. v3 requires Node 24 (compared to v2, which required Node 20).
  2. The behavior of version: min has changed between v2 and v3.
    • In v2, version: min would resolve to the minimum major/minor/patch, e.g. 1.10.0.
    • In v3, version: min resolves to the minimum major/minor but the latest patch, e.g. 1.10.11.
    • If you specifically want the minimum major/minor/patch under v3, you should specify version: min-patch. Note: v3 also adds the alias version: min-minor, which is equivalent to version: min.
  3. v3 will throw an error if x86_64 Julia binaries are requested on Apple Silicon macOS. (Under v2, this was a warning.) Under v3, if you specifically want to run x86_64 Julia binaries on Apple Silicon (under Rosetta 2), you must now opt-in by specifying the force-arch: true input.

Other Changes

We updated some dependencies, and we improved and updated the CI tooling on this repo.

Full Changelog
